narrative:
The model determined that you have an 82% probability of representing a bad credit risk. This high likelihood led directly to the denial of your loan application.

The three factors that most strongly influenced this outcome were the status of your checking account, the length of the loan you requested, and the level of your savings. Your checking account being in negative balance (<0 DM) was the strongest driver pushing the prediction toward bad credit risk. While only 12.6% of approved applicants have accounts in this state, the majority (59.2%) have no checking account at all. This negative status signaled higher risk to the model.

The 48-month duration you requested was the second most important factor and also pushed strongly toward denial. This is more than double the average length of 19 months among those who were approved, indicating the model viewed the extended repayment period as increasing the chance of default.

Your low savings balance (<100 DM) was the third key contributor, again moving the prediction toward bad credit. This is the most common savings level overall, but when combined with the negative checking account and long loan term, it reinforced the model's concern about your financial buffer.

To improve your chances on a future application, focus first on bringing your checking account balance positive, building up your savings, and considering a shorter loan duration if possible. Addressing these areas should meaningfully improve how a similar model evaluates your risk. (218 words)
